analysis.title: TAIWAN: Second Short Sell Ban Effective Tomorrow
key_insights: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) announced a second short sell ban in as many weeks, effective Friday, November 20, 2026, to stabilize its stock market.
The FSC cut the intraday cap on borrowed-share short sales from 3% to 1% of a stock's 30-day ADV.
Stocks down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted the following day. A similar measure was imposed in October 2022.
The November 9 round cut the borrowed-share cap from 30% to 3% and raised minimum short-sale margin from 90% to 130%. Margin is unchanged in the November 20 round.

The 2022 cycle tightened in steps (cap 30% to 20% to 10%, margin 90% to 100% to 120%) and restrictions were lifted Feb. 23-24, 2023. In the April 2025 tariff sell-off the cap and margin reverted May 26, 2025.
No end date has been announced for the current measures.
The November 9 round also encouraged listed companies to consider buybacks and hold investor briefings.
GS Asia Strategy downgraded Taiwan to Market Weight from Overweight and cut its 2027 TAIEX target to 50,000, which still implies 30% upside.
GS Asia Strategy says strong earnings remain supportive, but concentrated AI-capex risk, high valuation premiums and elevated volatility temper risk/reward.
Heavy foreign selling has been absorbed by retail and ETF inflows, while foreign ownership and domestic leverage remain elevated.
Within Taiwan, GS Asia Strategy recommends Quality Tech as core exposure, complemented tactically by dividend-supported AI Diversifiers.
